rules.rule: Salience is a stimulus property/priority signal; attentional capture is an observed control failure/priority shift. Do not merge.
Goal relevance, target template, and executive control are related components of top-down selection but require distinct measurements.
Novelty, surprise, and uncertainty may contribute to curiosity but none should be encoded as curiosity itself.
Subjective utility is distinct from affective valence and arousal.
In-group identification is a higher-order construct; self-definition and self-investment are separable dimensions and should remain queryable.
Integrity, benevolence, expertise, and competence can contribute to trustworthiness judgments but are not interchangeable with the integrated judgment.
Credibility cues influence judgments; they are not themselves trustworthiness.
Familiarity from exposure must not be upgraded to intimacy or attachment without direct relational evidence.
Observed sharing action and sharing intention remain separate due to imperfect intention-behavior correspondence.
Recommendation is an endorsement action; word-of-mouth evaluation is the valenced/evaluative communication content.
Prediction error is a learning signal; outcome-value updating is the resulting change in learned value representation.
Context-response association, cue-triggering, and automaticity are evidence about habit mechanisms but no single one is a complete habit diagnosis.
